use: One application coordinates requests, memory, models, tools and learning.
why: Makes ordering, authority and failure handling explicit without a full agent framework.
limit: Pin the runtime; implement and test lifecycle rules before adding framework complexity.

status: Baseline plan; isolated contract probe only
use: One local database stores source history, interpreted memory, evidence, revisions, jobs and operation results.
why: A shared transaction boundary keeps memory changes, exclusions and durable work consistent with a simple reviewer setup.
limit: Product migrations and recovery tests remain; reconsider the storage engine for multi-host or substantial concurrent writes.

use: Search permitted source text and memory projections for names, terms and explicit phrases.
why: Provides a lexical baseline and independent source retrieval when extraction misses useful information.
limit: Wording differences can reduce recall; evaluate lexical retrieval before introducing dense retrieval.

use: Validate input and model-output structure before memory admission or tool execution.
why: Typed contracts reject malformed values; application rules enforce ownership, evidence, scope and allowed transitions.
limit: Valid JSON and types do not establish factual truth, permission or correct interpretation.

use: Call the hosted model with timeouts, bounded retries and recorded usage.
why: Contains provider-specific behavior behind one replaceable interface shared by answering and learning.
limit: Implement explicit error handling; API retry policy cannot establish whether an external tool effect occurred.

status: User's provider/model-family choice; exact model pending
use: Interpret candidate memories and generate answers or permitted tool proposals from selected evidence.
why: Preserves the chosen provider while keeping memory truth and execution authority in application code.
limit: Verify model ID, context limits, structured outputs, tool support, quotas and costs; eligible context leaves local storage.

use: Encode permitted text locally and score stored vectors for meaning-based retrieval candidates.
why: May recover paraphrases; exact local scoring avoids a separate vector service in the initial design.
limit: Benchmark accuracy, languages, latency and storage; compare BGE-M3 only if useful. Vectors are not authoritative memory.

use: Connect supported identities and relationships with attribution, scope, time and evidence.
why: Supports bounded relationship expansion inside the same revision and exclusion rules as other memory.
limit: Matching names do not prove identity; unresolved identities remain separate until evidence supports resolution.

use: Process persisted learning jobs after permitted input is released; commit only against current revisions.
why: Keeps learning off ordinary answer latency while retaining progress across interruption and restart.
limit: Implement idempotency, attempt fencing, held-input rules, retries and recovery; stale workers must not restore forgotten knowledge.

use: Import records, query memory and inspect controls through the same core application.
why: Makes the complete backend path repeatable before investing in the final interface.
limit: CLI alone does not satisfy the assignment; a working normal-user interface remains required.

use: Expose imported dictation history, typed Hey Kivi requests, inspectable sources and ordinary-language memory controls.
why: Lets the mentor and reviewers experience the product while reusing one memory implementation.
limit: Choose web or desktop around the first journey; FastAPI and React are not selected dependencies.

status: Baseline boundary; first local effect proposed
use: Execute narrowly defined authorized operations and store observed outcomes separately from model claims.
why: Makes authority, exact arguments and uncertain effects reviewable before adding external connectors.
limit: Add MCP only for a selected integration; remembered requests never grant current execution authority.

use: Future alternatives for measured traversal, vector-scan or shared-cache requirements.
why: One local database and optional checked memory views keep the initial system simpler to operate and inspect.
limit: Add infrastructure only for demonstrated limits; any migration must revalidate ownership, exclusions, isolation and retry contracts.
